subject.title: [Bug]: Non-Anthropic models output tool calls as plain text '[tool: exec]' instead of tool_use blocks

question: When a provider returns only a bare marker such as `[tool: exec]` with no structured tool call or arguments, should OpenClaw retry/fallback/block, suppress and warn, or attempt a constrained recovery?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the safe runtime response is a provider/tool-policy choice because executing a bare marker lacks arguments and fallback/retry behavior changes existing provider routing.

options.title: Choose explicit recovery policy
options.body: Keep the issue open and decide a bounded behavior such as retry/fallback/blocking or warning before implementing tests and runtime changes.

options.title: Diagnostics-only mitigation
options.body: Treat bare markers as non-executable, suppress visible leakage where safe, and add provider diagnostics without changing fallback execution behavior.

options.title: Provider documentation only
options.body: Document affected models as unreliable for tool-enabled fallback use and leave runtime behavior unchanged until stronger live evidence exists.

recommendation.title: Choose explicit recovery policy
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open and decide a bounded behavior such as retry/fallback/blocking or warning before implementing tests and runtime changes.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent Koc is the strongest recent history match for provider/tool-call repair and release-state code carrying this behavior.
